answer: In an agent market buying marble from a karst quarry near an inlet, each seller identity must lock a $1,000 bond for 30 days before bidding, with one active bid per bond. Creating 100 fake sellers therefore ties up $100,000; splitting funds among new names cannot create extra bidding slots without extra collateral. The lock makes flooding the market costly through capital requirements and forgone interest, though a wealthy attacker can still pay.
